title: Hammurabi law 196, in King's English, puts out the eye of the man who puts out an eye
summary: King's Hammurabi says: if a man puts out another man's eye, his eye shall be put out.
body: Law 196 in L. W. King's English of the Code of Hammurabi says that if a man put out the eye of another man, his eye shall be put out. The next laws on the same page set a different payment when the injured person is a freed man or a slave. The equal penalty is stated for a man and another man, not for every person. The wording on the page includes: "shall be cut off. 195. If a son strike his father, his hands shall be hewn off. 196. If a man put out the eye of another man, his eye shall be put out. [ An eye for an eye ] 197. If he break another man's bone, his bone shall be broken. 198. If he put out the eye of a freed man, or break the bone of a freed man, he shall pay one gold mina. 199.
